frequency_question: How often does a central bank deploy an incremental cash reserve ratio instrument during periods of acute banking sector liquidity surpluses within a defined short calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes official central bank deployment of secondary or incremental reserve requirements specifically designed to mop up excess liquidity. Excludes standard, permanent changes to baseline reserve requirements.
provenance_note: 2 cases named, 4 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.0x)
coverage_note: 2 named episodes of iCRR deployment; approximately 4 distinct periods of extreme liquidity overhang requiring extraordinary measures in India since 2004.
known_gaps: Does not fully account for subtle shifts in modern liquidity management frameworks favoring variable rate reverse repos over quantity-based restrictions, though iCRR remains in the toolkit.
skeleton: RBI policy interventions during systemic liquidity surges over the last two decades, decomposed into distinct liquidity glut episodes requiring extraordinary sterilization tools.
multiplier: 2 occurrences out of roughly 4 major systemic liquidity overhang episodes in the jurisdiction equals 50 percent base frequency.
validity_reason: Central bank institutional memory and regulatory toolkits evolve slowly over multi-year horizons, keeping structural liquidity management precedents relevant for at least two years.
